attempts.summary: Built a WireGuard site-to-site tunnel joining node1's (VyOS) private LAN (10.10.1.0/24, hosting node3) and node2's (OPNsense) private LAN (10.10.2.0/24, hosting node4) across their transit link (10.10.12.0/30). Discovered the physical NIC pairings via arping/ping (node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 transit; node1 eth2<->node3 enp8s0; node2 vtnet2<->node4 enp8s0), assigned static addressing, stood up a WireGuard tunnel (10.10.99.0/30) between the routers with reciprocal AllowedIPs covering each private subnet, added OPNsense filter/interface-assignment and VyOS static-route glue needed for the OPNsense WG plugin's route-derivation quirks, and added specific (non-default-route-clobbering) static routes on node3/node4 pointing at their router for the peer's private subnet. Verified bidirectional host-to-host ping (node3<->node4) traveling only through the tunnel. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes (VyOS `reboot`, OPNsense `/sbin/reboot`, RHEL `systemctl reboot`), confirming a changed OS-native boot marker (kernel boot_id / kern.boottime) each time and proving post-restart recovery of interfaces, the WireGuard handshake, static routes, and end-to-end node3<->node4 connectivity before moving to the next node.
